The test `test_TimeseriesGenerator` checks whether the length of a `TimeseriesGenerator` object is correctly calculated given different parameters. However, the test fails with an assertion error when calling the `__len__` method on the `data_gen` object in the line where it is asserted that `len(data_gen) == 6`. 

Following the execution path, we find that the issue lies in the calculation of the length in the `__len__` method. The `start_index` and `end_index` parameters are used to calculate the number of batches. However, when `end_index` is not set (i.e., it defaults to None), it causes an undefined behavior. Consequently, incorrect values are passed to the `np.ceil` function, leading to a wrong calculation of the length.

Consequently, when `start_index=10`, `end_index=None`, and `batch_size=2`, the division in the `__len__` method results in a non-integer value, causing an assertion error because it is compared with an integer 6. 

The correct calculation should consider that when `end_index` is not set, the end index of the sequence should be set to half of the total number of elements (i.e., `(self.start_index + len(self.data)) / 2`). This would ensure that the length of the `TimeseriesGenerator` object is correctly calculated given different parameters.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
